places.name: Sir John Soane's Museum
places.note: An architect's house turned into a cabinet of light. Domes, mirrors and borrowed daylight do more here than any ornament. Go on a weekday morning, before the queue.

places.name: Barbican Conservatory
places.note: A tropical glasshouse wrapped around a theatre fly tower. Brutalism and banana leaves in the same frame. Open on selected days only, so book ahead.

places.name: St Dunstan-in-the-East
places.note: A bombed Wren church left as a ruin and let the garden in. Ivy climbs the tracery where the glass used to be. Best at lunchtime, when the City empties its offices.

places.name: Leighton House
places.note: A Victorian painter's studio-house with a gold-domed Arab Hall at its heart. Tiles, still water, a single fountain. The quietest room in west London.

places.name: Kyoto Garden
places.note: A Japanese garden folded into an English park: tiered waterfall, koi, maples. Pair it with Leighton House, five minutes' walk away.

places.name: The Wallace Collection
places.note: Old Masters still hanging in the townhouse they were collected for. Coloured silk walls, Fragonard's swing, armour by the roomful. Free, and never crowded.

places.name: Daunt Books
places.note: An Edwardian bookshop with a long oak gallery and a skylight. Shelved by country, so you browse the way you travel.

places.name: Dennis Severs' House
places.note: A Georgian house staged as if its family just left the room. Candlelight, ticking clocks, half-eaten bread. Visits are silent; keep it that way.

places.name: London Mithraeum
places.note: A Roman temple rebuilt seven metres down, beneath Foster's Bloomberg building. Light and sound rebuild the walls in haze. Free; book a slot.

places.name: Isokon Building
places.note: Britain's first modernist block of flats, white and ocean-liner sleek. Gropius and Breuer both lived here. A small gallery tells the story on seasonal weekends.

places.name: Sessions Arts Club
places.note: Dinner in the old judges' dining room of an 18th-century courthouse, its plaster left beautifully undone. Art on the walls, seasonal plates. Book well ahead.

places.name: National Theatre
places.note: Lasdun's terraced concrete on the river, all decks and fly towers. Walk the terraces at dusk even without a ticket.

places.name: Tate Modern
places.note: A power station turned gallery; the Turbine Hall is the city's largest room. Climb the Blavatnik tower for the view.

places.name: Serpentine South Gallery
places.note: A 1930s tea pavilion turned gallery in the park. Each summer a different architect builds a pavilion on the lawn.

places.name: Design Museum
places.note: A 1960s hyperbolic copper roof sheltering a new museum inside. Look up from the atrium stair.

places.name: V&A Cast Courts
places.note: Plaster copies of Trajan's Column and Michelangelo's David, gathered under two Victorian skylit halls. Then the garden café.

places.name: Royal Academy of Arts
places.note: A Palladian courtyard off Piccadilly, linked by Chipperfield to the old Senate House behind. The Summer Exhibition is part of London's year.

places.name: Kenwood House
places.note: Robert Adam's library and a Rembrandt self-portrait, at the top of Hampstead Heath. Free, with a walk across the heath to get there.

places.name: Highgate Cemetery
places.note: Victorian catacombs and an Egyptian avenue overgrown with ivy. The West side is seen on guided tours; the East is open to wander.

places.name: 2 Willow Road
places.note: Ernő Goldfinger's own modernist house, still furnished as he lived in it, art collection and all. Small timed tours.

places.name: Eltham Palace
places.note: An Art Deco mansion of the 1930s grafted onto a medieval great hall. The circular entrance hall is pure Hollywood.

places.name: Trellick Tower
places.note: Goldfinger's brutalist tower with its detached lift core and sky bridges. Best seen from Golborne Road.

places.name: Alexandra Road Estate
places.note: A curving street of stepped concrete terraces from the 1970s, quietly utopian. Walk Rowley Way end to end.

places.name: Lloyd's Building
places.note: Rogers's machine for insurance: lifts, ducts and stairs on the outside, in stainless steel. Look from Leadenhall Market.

places.name: Postman's Park
places.note: A small garden with Watts's wall of glazed tiles remembering ordinary people who died saving others. Deeply moving.

places.name: Kew Gardens
places.note: The Victorian Palm House and the restored Temperate House, two of the great glasshouses. Give it a whole day.

places.name: Columbia Road Flower Market
places.note: A Sunday-only flower market on a street of small shops. Come at the end, when the sellers cut their prices.

places.name: St. JOHN
places.note: Nose-to-tail cooking in a whitewashed former smokehouse. Bone marrow on toast, then a madeleine from the bakery.

places.name: John Sandoe Books
places.note: Three small 18th-century houses packed with books, chosen by people who read them. Ask for a recommendation.

places.name: Liberty
places.note: A mock-Tudor store built from the timbers of two old warships, galleries round a timbered atrium. Prints, haberdashery and the scent hall.

places.name: The Connaught Bar
places.note: A sleek, silvered Mayfair bar where martinis are mixed at a trolley by your table. Formal and worth it.
